n: This lecture is the second part on precursors. The outline: ergotamine, ergometrine, lysergic acid and anthranilic acid, and the methods of their analysis. These substances are on the list of precursors and are the principal substances in obtaining narcotic drugs. Key terms: precursor, ergot alkaloids, LSD, Ehrlich test, TLC and UV spectrum.

Precursors are substances that are included in the list of precursors and controlled in Uzbekistan. They are used to prepare narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. The glossary repeats the same definition: substances included in the list and whose circulation is controlled.

Legal basis. On the basis of the decisions of the 1988 UN Single Convention, 26 substances have been placed under international control as precursors. On 19 August 1999 the Law “On Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances” was adopted in Uzbekistan. The law regulates social relations concerning the circulation of narcotic, intoxicating and precursor substances. The malaka material states that this law was adopted on the basis of the UN conventions of 1961, 1971 and 1988.

t: The list and its two groups
n: The chemical substances on the list are conventionally divided into two groups. Group 1: substances used in the synthesis of narcotic drugs and making up the larger part of their chemical formula. Group 2: substances that play an auxiliary but principal role in clandestine preparation. That is, the first group is a structural component, and the second performs an auxiliary function.

Table 18, first part. The list consists of 26 entries; substances marked with an asterisk are also given in the table. Acetic acid anhydride is the precursor of methaqualone and heroin, and anthranilic acid of 4-methylaminorex and methaqualone. Lysergic acid and N-methylephedrine: LSD and methcathinone are prepared. Pseudoephedrine is indicated for pervitin.

Table 18, second part. Ergotamine and ergometrine, that is, ergonovine, are indicated in the table for preparing LSD. Ephedrine is indicated for methcathinone, and phenylacetic acid for preparing MDA and its derivatives.

Table 19 divides precursors into starting substances, reagents and solvents. Starting substances: anthranilic, lysergic and phenylacetic acids, ergometrine, pseudoephedrine and others. Reagents: acetic acid anhydride, red phosphorus, potassium permanganate, sulphuric and hydrochloric acids. Solvents: acetone, methyl ethyl ketone, that is, 2-butanone, toluene and diethyl ether.

Why are ergot precursors controlled? Because ergotamine, ergometrine and lysergic acid are the principal substances in obtaining lysergic acid diethylamide, that is, LSD, which has a hallucinogenic effect. Anthranilic acid is used as the principal substance in the synthesis of 4-methylaminorex and methaqualones. That is, these substances are regarded as principal substances in obtaining narcotic drugs.

Structure and properties of ergotamine. Ergotamine, synonyms femergin and gynergen, formula C33H35N5O5; an ergot alkaloid. It is a hygroscopic crystalline powder with the properties of a base; melting point 212-214 °C. It does not dissolve in water, dissolves in ethyl alcohol, and dissolves well in chloroform.

Hydrolysis of ergotamine. Under alkaline conditions ergotamine is hydrolysed. Hydrolysis products: lysergic acid, L-proline, L-phenylalanine, pyruvic acid and ammonia. For this reason lysergic acid also occurs as a breakdown product of ergotamine.

Ergometrine is an odourless white crystalline powder. It is slightly soluble in water and alcohol. Ergometrine is one of the principal ergot alkaloids; it increases the tone of the uterine muscles and speeds their contraction. By comparison: ergotamine is a hygroscopic crystalline powder with a melting point of 212-214 °C, while ergometrine is an odourless white crystalline powder.

t: Isolation of ergot alkaloids from a biological specimen
n: Isolation of ergot alkaloids from a biological specimen. They are extracted by soaking in a water-acetone mixture, ratio 5:3. Acetone is also on the list of precursors: it is both a laboratory solvent and a controlled substance. After isolation, TLC, UV spectrum and HPLC methods are used; “Silufol” plates are used in TLC and “Milichrom” 4-A in HPLC.

In thin-layer chromatography, ready-made “Silufol” plates containing silica gel are used as the plate. Mobile phase for ergometrine: n-butanol, n-hexane and 25% ammonia solution, ratio 20:15:0.5. For ergotamine: acetone, chloroform and water, ratio 3:1:0.5.

Visualising reagents. With a 10% solution of silver nitrate a brown colour forms. With a 1% solution of potassium permanganate, ergometrine and ergotamine give an orange product. With a solution of potassium dichromate in 20% sulphuric acid a blue product forms. With a 0.5% solution of p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde in 65% sulphuric acid, ergometrine and ergotamine give blue.

Identification by UV spectrum. Ergometrine maleate in water gives a maximum at 311 nm and a minimum at 269 nm. Ergotamine hydrotartrate in water gives a maximum at 318 nm and a minimum at 272 nm. Dihydroergotamine mesylate in ethanol gives a maximum at 280 nm. The table gives the maximum and minimum for all three substances.

HPLC and quantitative methods. For qualitative and quantitative determination, a “Milichrom” 4-A microcolumn liquid chromatograph with a UV spectrophotometric detector is used. In the extraction-photometric method, ergot alkaloids react with tropaeolin 00; the absorbance of the coloured product formed is measured. In the spectrophotometric method, the salts are dissolved in water and the absorbance is measured.

In spectrophotometric quantitative analysis, the absorbance is measured at different wavelengths depending on the substance. For ergometrine maleate at 311 nm, for ergotamine tartrate at 314 nm, and for ergotoxine at 320 nm.

Lysergic acid forms the basis of most ergot alkaloids. It is a poisonous narcotic drug with a hallucinogenic effect; LSD, that is, the diethylamide, is obtained from it. Lysergic acid is a white crystalline powder; poorly soluble in water, readily soluble in alkalis.

Toxicity of lysergic acid and LSD. Its diethylamide, that is, LSD, is obtained from lysergic acid; the lethal dose of LSD is 0.0002 g/kg. LSD is a poisonous narcotic drug with a hallucinogenic effect, and lysergic acid is its precursor. For this reason both the precursor and the product are under strict control.

The Ehrlich test for lysergic acid. In the Ehrlich test, a sample containing lysergic acid gives a violet colour. Preparation of the reagent: 2 g of n-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde is dissolved in 100 ml of 20% hydrochloric acid solution. In the malaka lecture this reaction is given as the van Urk, that is, Ehrlich, reaction for the ergot derivatives of LSD.

Fluorescence of lysergic acid and TLC. Under a UV lamp lysergic acid gives blue fluorescence. In TLC the dry residue is dissolved in methanol and applied to a silica gel plate. System: chloroform, acetone, ethanol and 25% ammonia solution, ratio 20:20:3:1. When Ehrlich reagent is sprayed, a violet spot with Rf=0.57 forms.

t: Lysergic acid: UV and IR spectrum
n: Spectra of lysergic acid. In the UV spectrum, the solution in alkali absorbs maximally at 310 nm, and the solution in hydrochloric acid at 315 nm. In the IR spectrum, in a KBr pellet, absorption bands are observed at 1626, 1307, 1136, 1066, 1212 and 749 cm-1. Remember: in the textbook the IR values are called “wavelengths”, but they are given in units of cm-1.

Anthranilic acid, that is, o-aminobenzoic acid, is a white crystalline powder; it melts at 145 °C. It dissolves in water, alcohol, benzene, diethyl ether and acetic acid. It is used as the principal substance in the synthesis of 4-methylaminorex and methaqualones.

t: Anthranilic acid: Ehrlich test and fluorescence
n: Anthranilic acid forms a yellowish-lemon colour in the Ehrlich test. Its salts with alkali metals and mineral acids dissolve well in water. Solutions of the salts give light-blue fluorescence in UV light.

Inner complexes of anthranilic acid. In solutions in acetic acid, at pH 2.5-5, it forms inner complexes with salts of cadmium, cobalt, copper, nickel, zinc, lead and mercury. These complexes are slightly soluble in water. This property is used in the gravimetric determination of metals.

Other reactions of anthranilic acid. By diazotisation it is converted to o-diazobenzoic acid; on irradiation with UV light it is converted to dehydrobenzene. With a solution of Cu(II) salts in acetic acid it gives a bright green precipitate; m-aminobenzoic acid, by contrast, gives light blue. On distillation it decarboxylates and is converted to aniline.

t: Amount of anthranilic acid; N-acetylanthranilic acid
n: The amount of anthranilic acid is determined by the UV spectrophotometric method. N-acetylanthranilic acid is indicated in the table as a precursor of methaqualone. In the malaka material, N-acetylanthranilic acid is described as a white or whitish-yellow crystalline powder, and it is said to be used in the synthesis of mecloqualone and methaqualone.

Ephedrine and pseudoephedrine as precursors. In the table, ephedrine is indicated as the precursor of methcathinone, and pseudoephedrine as the precursor of pervitin. Ephedrine and its stereoisomer pseudoephedrine occur in the ephedra plant and can also be obtained synthetically. Ephedrone is formed by drug addicts from ephedrine by oxidation with potassium permanganate and acetic acid at 50-60 °C.

Identification of ephedrine and ephedrone. With Dragendorff reagent, both ephedrine and ephedrone give dark red needle-shaped crystals. With a 1% solution of Reinecke salt, ephedrine forms four-sided reddish-pink crystals, while ephedrone gives thin straight-edged crystals. In TLC, with chloroform-acetone 48:2 and ninhydrin, ephedrine Rf=0.28, ephedrone Rf=0.71.
Phenylacetic acid is included in the list of precursors. The substance prepared with the precursor: MDA and its derivatives. Phenylacetic acid is listed in table 19 among the starting substances.

A reminder about sulphuric and hydrochloric acids. Sulphuric acid, H2SO4, is used as a reagent in obtaining narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. H2SO4 gives a white precipitate, BaSO4, with barium salts; its amount is determined by the neutralisation method. HCl gives a white precipitate, AgCl, with silver nitrate in an acidic medium; its amount is also determined by the neutralisation method.

We compare lysergic and anthranilic acids. Lysergic acid is a white crystalline powder; poorly soluble in water, readily soluble in alkalis; it gives blue fluorescence under a UV lamp. Anthranilic acid is also a white crystalline powder; it melts at 145 °C; it dissolves in water, alcohol and benzene. In the Ehrlich test lysergic acid gives violet, and anthranilic acid yellowish-lemon.

t: Scheme for analysis of ergot alkaloids
n: Scheme for analysis of ergot alkaloids. Isolation: the biological specimen is soaked in a water-acetone mixture, ratio 5:3. Identification: TLC on a “Silufol” plate, visualising reagents and UV spectrum; qualitative and quantitative determination by HPLC with “Milichrom” 4-A. The amount is found by the extraction-photometric method, with tropaeolin 00, or by the spectrophotometric method.

t: Rules for preparing the sample for analysis
n: Rules for preparing the sample for analysis. If the suspected substance is present in a small amount, all of it must be submitted for analysis. From a powdered substance a few crystals are taken; if repeat analysis is needed, twice as many are taken. Tablets and solid substances are first crushed with a spatula and analysed; a capsule is carefully opened. Plant raw material and tobacco products are first crushed and analysed.

Practical case: unknown powder. In the case from the textbook, an unknown crystalline powder causing hallucinations has been brought for forensic chemical examination. The preliminary analysis gave an azo dye reaction; the solution must be set out. Table columns: type of problem, causes of origin and ways of resolution.

Review questions. First: what substances are called precursors? Second: what is the use and narcological significance of ergotamine, and the significance of chromatographic methods? Third: what are the methods of analysing sulphuric and hydrochloric acids, and what is known about anthranilic acid?

Glossary. Precursors are substances that are included in the list, controlled and used for preparing drugs. A preparation is a mixture containing one or several narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances. Polydrug addiction is the chronic intake of two or more kinds of narcotic drugs. The table also gives the terms drug addiction and toxicomania.

Conclusion. Ergotamine, ergometrine, lysergic acid and anthranilic acid are the principal precursors in the synthesis of narcotic drugs. For ergot alkaloids, water-acetone extraction, ratio 5:3, TLC, UV spectrum and HPLC are used; for lysergic acid, the Ehrlich test, fluorescence and Rf=0.57. Anthranilic acid gives a yellowish-lemon colour in the Ehrlich test, light-blue fluorescence in UV, and forms inner complexes.
